target: fatal accidents involving Boeing commercial jets

evidence.scope: global commercial aviation under IATA methodology
evidence.observation: IATA reports ten fatal accidents in 2016, five jet and five turboprop in later IATA summaries. Critically, its fatality count covers people onboard and explicitly does not count people killed on the ground or on other aircraft outside its criteria.
evidence.use: annual-scope evidence with explicit external-fatality limitation

evidence.observation: EASA's wider 2016 review explicitly names FlyDubai B737-800 and Emirates B777-300 among fatal CAT aeroplane accidents, demonstrating why onboard-only fatality accounting is insufficient for BSFM.
Commercial air transport; FlyDubai Boeing 737-800; 62 onboard fatalities.

evidence.publisher: UAE GCAA Air Accident Investigation Sector
evidence.observation: Emirates scheduled passenger flight UAE521, Boeing 777-31H A6-EMW, serial 32700; all occupants survived but one firefighter was fatally injured; occurrence classified as an Annex 13 accident.

open_items: Enumerate all five 2016 fatal jet accidents under IATA and map each to Boeing/non-Boeing target membership.
Reconcile IATA onboard-only fatality accounting against EASA/Boeing sources that preserve external fatalities.
Demonstrate that no additional Boeing commercial-jet accident qualifies solely through external fatalities.
Keep target taxonomy consistent with 2017 ACT and other external-fatality cases.

completeness_assessment.reason: Two qualifying Boeing candidates are supported, including the external-fatality-only EK521 case, but IATA's onboard-only fatality accounting cannot alone exhaust the BSFM target and the full five-fatal-jet mapping is not yet complete.
